title: Megabonk/Vampire Survivors inspired PSX style parody game (Opus 5.5 + Godot)
author: Xipha-Softworks
selftext:
Hi all! Fairly new to whole Claude/Ai game development thing and have been using it to build my own megabonk/vampire survivors style game using the whole era of PSX/PS1 as the driving force for the aesthetics. Very much going for the parody vibe, built in Godot.

Mostly made using Opus 5.5 on Medium effort with Blender MCP to help with modelling. Originally used Blockbench to make my environments but they looked a little too basic, Blender was used for the current version of the level. The two playable characters were built in Tripo3D then textured in Blender directly but have since moved to a local model for the WIP characters currently in production.

If you'd like to try it out I have a demo live on itch: [https://xiphasoftworks.itch.io/demo-disc-survivors](https://xiphasoftworks.itch.io/demo-disc-survivors)

It's playable in browser and also downloadable, happy to answer any questions regarding my workflow or how I achieved certain things.

The characters are obviously parodies of Lara Croft and Crash Bandicoot, they probably are a bit too close to their counterparts atm so likely down the line I'll look at changing them up a little but still a very clear parody of those characters.

comments.author: Lambisexual
comments.body: How did you get the models? Especially rigged properly. Cause the Lara model seemed to be able to aim her guns independently.

replies.author: Xipha-Softworks
replies.body: Both done with Tripo3D! Exported and then rigged in blender directly. The rigging was the easy part, making the animations look somewhat decent took longer. Originally used some free mixamo animations but they didn't really fit so just tweaked and tweaked till it reached a decent level. Still needs work!

comments.author: Reasonable-Reason901
comments.body: I love this. Where is the music from?

replies.author: Xipha-Softworks
replies.body: Generated with Suno AI! Really cool site that does some great sounding music, the game has a mix of suno and some free open music atm

replies.author: Reasonable-Reason901
replies.body:
Ohh nice I use suno too for my game. I don’t have any plans to make a retro style game but would love to have some tracks like this just for messing around with, do you have the prompt you used for this track?

Edit: not sure if retro is even the right word here but there’s something nostalgic about it that I really enjoy in the tune

replies.author: Xipha-Softworks
replies.body:
Sure do! 

Here it is:   
  
**Instrumental PS1-era 32-bit console menu music, mid-tempo funk-rock groove around 110 BPM, major-key and playful, warmly welcoming with cheeky retro game-menu energy, Open with a two-bar bright synth sweep and cymbal swell, then settle into punchy laid-back drums with shuffled hi-hat and buoyant warm slap bass, Repeat a catchy heroic lead melody shared by bright synth and clean electric guitar, with marimba and steel drum accents, soft pads, and a subtle adventurous jungle-flute color, In the second half add restrained brass stabs and harmonized leads for a gentle lift, keeping the groove relaxed and easy to sit with, Slightly crunchy lo-fi 32-bit console texture, clear melodic hook, seamless loop ending without a fade**

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
>The characters are obviously parodies of Lara Croft and Crash Bandicoot, they probably are a bit too close to their counterparts atm so likely down the line I'll look at changing them up a little but still a very clear parody of those characters.

  
Just FYI, a parody must still be transformative to be protected. It has to be a demonstrable critique or joke aimed at the material, where the focus of the art is on the critique/joke, not the IP or trade dress.

If you want an in-depth dissection of how the highest court in the US looks at parody defenses, read Jack Daniel's Properties, Inc. v. VIP Products LLC (or have an LLM give you a brief overview of the case).

comments.body: What's the logic behind tara croft shooting at 2 different enemies? Does each gun just shoot the closest enemy to that gun? Looks cool

replies.author: Xipha-Softworks
replies.body: At the moment she just shoots one target at a time, Whatever hand she primarily shooting from changes depending which is closer. The goal is to eventually make it shoot independently though at different targets!
